classification.difficultyReason: Sketch a normal distribution and combine empirical-rule regions for symmetric and asymmetric intervals.

content.prompt: A normal distribution has mean 65 and standard deviation 4.

answer.short: A symmetric bell curve centred at 65, with axis ticks at 53, 57, 61, 65, 69, 73 and 77.
answer.worked: Mark the mean, $65$, at the centre. Each standard deviation is $4$, so mark $61,57,53$ to the left and $69,73,77$ to the right. Sketch a symmetric bell curve above the axis.

spec.description: Symmetric bell curve with a horizontal axis arrowed at both ends and seven equally spaced labelled ticks. No vertical axis or shading. Decorative source blue is replaced by ordinary black.
spec.mathematics: Mean 65; standard deviation 4; ticks at the mean and one, two and three standard deviations on either side.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer only; leave the student sketch region blank.

children.prompt: Find the percentage of data between:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}57&=65-2(4)\\73&=65+2(4)\end{aligned}$$
The interval is within two standard deviations of the mean, so it contains approximately $95\%$ of the data.
$61=65-4$, so the interval runs from one standard deviation below the mean to the mean. By symmetry, its percentage is $68\%\div2=34\%$.
$77=65+3(4)$, so the interval runs from the mean to three standard deviations above the mean. By symmetry, its percentage is $99.7\%\div2=49.85\%$.

$57=65-2(4)$ and $69=65+4$. The interval runs from two standard deviations below the mean to one above it.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage}&=13.5\%+34\%+34\%\\&=81.5\%\end{aligned}$$

$61=65-4$ and $73=65+2(4)$. The interval runs from one standard deviation below the mean to two above it.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage}&=34\%+34\%+13.5\%\\&=81.5\%\end{aligned}$$
